hypothesis: A higher Korean Customs first-20-day semiconductor export YoY, available only from the first US session strictly after the official portal registered date, signals stronger near-term semiconductor demand. Conditional on original Stage1 39 inputs and common month/age controls it should predict lower cash-minus-SOXX next-five-open-interval value; the candidate's added standardized coefficient is expected negative.
distinctness: The Customs provisional early20 release is earlier and issuer-composition-independent relative to previously failed delayed global SIA sales and TSMC realized monthly revenue. This version uses only reported raw semiconductor YoY, not a working-day-adjusted or consensus surprise, and a matched Stage1 cash H5 receiver; no route or sign search.

receiver.baseline: Original Stage1 39 inputs plus common sin/cos calendar-month phase and source age in actual Qlib sessions. Identical median imputation, StandardScaler, Ridge(alpha=1) on only common mature source-known rows.
receiver.candidate: The identical baseline plus one carried reported raw KCS semiconductor export YoY percent. No clipping or sign reversal, including 2026 extreme values.
receiver.second_control: Mean of the identical training labels, no fit.
receiver.label: Negative sum of log(1+SOXX forward open-to-open return) across exactly five consecutive native Qlib sessions from frozen parent frame; available only after the fifth interval matures.
receiver.decision_clock: KCS map joins to the trade session derived from frozen parent timing.decision_at, not the prior signal-date close. Portal-date strict-next-Qlib-session mapping is conservative but current source byte vintage remains unqualified.
